explanation: Swimmers in the 1,500 m freestyle swim 30 lengths, turning at the wall 29 times. Many club and school pools are 25 m long, which is why short-course races exist.

claims.text: An Olympic-size swimming pool is 50 metres long.
Olympic pools are not 25, 75 or 100 metres long.
A 1,500 metre race in a 50 metre pool is 30 lengths, with 29 turns.
Short-course swimming competitions are held in 25 metre pools, a common length for club and school pools.

writerNotes: Subtopic: swimming. Written as an easy item, because the sport pool is short of easy items. lint: clean. claims: four, all high for numbers. datasets: none covers pool sizes; World Aquatics facility rules. c3 is arithmetic on c1 (1500 / 50 = 30 lengths, 29 turns between them). rivalTest: 25 m is the planted confusion (short course); 75 and 100 m are wrong under any reading. Argued against the key: a few older pools were 33 1/3 yards or 55 yards, but 'Olympic-size' means 50 m. Key sits second in ascending order (X34 spread). volatility: evergreen. regional: worldwide. style: Oxford spelling, explanation of 30 words. myths: screened. mystery and encore: not applicable. doubts: none.

evidence.restatement: World Aquatics facility rules require a long-course competition pool, the kind used at the Olympics, to measure 50 m between the end walls.

claimResults.note: Answered 50 metres cold. Long-course (Olympic) pools are 50 m; this is the defining spec. Both-pass certain rule under memo 18.

evidence.restatement: An Olympic pool is neither 25 m (that is short course), 75 m nor 100 m long.

claimResults.note: 25 m is the short-course length and the likeliest wrong pick; 75 m and 100 m are not competition pool lengths. All definitely wrong.

evidence.restatement: Thirty lengths need a turn at the end of every length except the final one, so 29 turns.

claimResults.note: Arithmetic on c1: 30 lengths, and turns = lengths minus one = 29.

evidence.restatement: Short-course events, including the short-course world championships, are swum in 25 m pools, the usual size for many club and school pools.

claimResults.note: Short course means 25 m by definition in World Aquatics rules; 25 m pools are the commonest training size.

evidence.restatement: The standard long-course pool used at the Olympics and World Championships measures 50 m end to end (25 m wide).

claimResults.note: Rival test: 25 m is a short-course pool, not an Olympic one; 75 and 100 m do not exist in competition. 'Long' is length, so width cannot muddy it. Confirmed directly (memo 18).

evidence.restatement: No Olympic pool is 25, 75 or 100 m in length.

claimResults.note: 25 m pools host short-course events only.
30 lengths, and one fewer turn than lengths, so 29 turns (the finish is not a turn).

evidence.restatement: Short-course meets use 25 m pools, which are the usual size for clubs and schools.

editor.reason: A and B pass. Easy anchor item; 50 m and the 30 lengths, 29 turns arithmetic confirmed by both.

stem: How long is an Olympic-size swimming pool?
